overall: Atlanta is opening the morning completely overcast (OVC) with a very low ceiling of just 91m (~300 feet) and a high dewpoint of 69°F, which has kept overnight temperatures nearly stationary around 73–74°F through 8am. Despite sunrise having occurred well before the 07:52 observation, the current temp is 71.1°F with a slightly negative velocity (-0.5°F/hr) and no meaningful warming trend — the dense cloud deck is heavily suppressing early heating. The running max of 73.4°F was actually set at midnight, a notable inversion of the typical diurnal pattern.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are tightly clustered in the 85–87°F range (ECMWF=86.0, HRRR=85.2, NBM=86.4), sitting modestly below the NWS text forecast of 88°F — a small but consistent model-vs-text gap. The META model (most reliable) heavily concentrates probability in the 86–87°F bucket at 48.7%, while the INTRADAY model leans slightly warmer (88–89°F at 30%) based on climatological rebound from morning cloud suppression; the OVC conditions this early are the key source of disagreement between those two signals.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely outcome is a daily high in the 86–87°F range, anchored by the strong META model consensus (48.7%) and tight NWP agreement around 85.5–86.4°F. The critical wildcard is how quickly the OVC deck breaks: the NWS 'mostly sunny' forecast implies expected afternoon clearing, which would allow normal peak heating around 16–17h ET per NWP timing models. If clouds clear by midday, the upper tail (88–89°F, ~20%) is reachable; if clouds linger or precip fires early from the 20% afternoon storm chance, the high could stay near 84–85°F. Confidence is moderate — the model consensus is tight but morning conditions are currently running notably behind the forecast warming curve.
